In [[mathematics]], the '''tensor representations''' of the [[general linear group]] are those that are obtained by taking finitely many [[tensor product]]s of the [[fundamental representation]] and its dual.  The irreducible factors of such a representation are also called tensor representations, and can be obtained by applying [[Schur functor]]s (associated to [[Young tableaux]]).  These coincide with the [[rational representation]]s of the general linear group.

More generally, a [[matrix group]] is any subgroup of the general linear group.  A tensor representation of a matrix group is any representation that is contained in a tensor representation of the general linear group.  For example, the [[orthogonal group]] O(''n'') admits a tensor representation on the space of all trace-free symmetric tensors of order two.  For orthogonal groups, the tensor representations are contrasted with the [[spin representation]]s.
